paragraphs: The Tatars evoke the mounted armies of Central Asia, where Timur built the Timurid Empire. In the Tamerlane campaign, burning camel loads become an unlikely answer to the elephants of India.
The Flaming Camel carries that scene into the battlefield: a pack animal laden with straw, sent forward as a weapon.
Instead of trading blows, the Flaming Camel explodes when it attacks, damaging nearby enemies and sacrificing itself. Its blast is especially dangerous to mounted units and elephants.
Reaching the target is everything. Surviving the approach and meeting dense enemy formations decide how much damage a wave can deliver.
